title: [Mouse Pointer Crosshairs] Gliding cursor - additional settings to improve accessibility and convenience
author: Ded10c

status.label: Actionable design candidate
status.detail: The enhancement provides concrete accessibility scenarios and separable behavior changes, but it still requires a full design pass before any implementation approval.

next_action.label: Queue full design investigation
next_action.reason: Investigate the gliding state machine, settings surface, multi-monitor coordinates, and accessible speed/direction controls before exposing approve_design.

judgment.rationale: The report defines specific limitations in the current gliding cursor and concrete desired behaviors—relative origin, selectable starting display, and runtime speed/direction controls—with enough acceptance context for design investigation.
evidence: The current absolute origin leaves negative-coordinate monitor space unreachable and increases travel time for distant targets.
The request explains how relative positioning and selectable displays support distinct accessibility workflows.
Current implementation in MousePointerCrosshairs/dllmain.cpp uses a fixed multi-stage gliding state machine and fixed travel/delay settings, so the requested behaviors have identifiable ownership.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a full fork-side design investigation; keep stage design_in_progress and expose no approve_design action yet.

issue_context.summary: Gliding Cursor currently starts from a fixed main-display origin and uses fixed movement behavior; the proposal adds relative starts, monitor selection, and live speed/direction controls for broader accessibility use.
known_information: The fixed origin prevents reaching positions with negative X coordinates on left-side monitors.
The reporter describes relative and display-selectable start modes as separate options.
The requested speed and reverse controls are intended to help users correct overshoot without restarting.
Issue #41879 also requests direction and multi-screen improvements, but it does not cover the complete origin and control model described here.
inferences: The work can likely be split into origin/display policy and runtime-control increments, but a design must verify how the existing staged activation sequence should evolve.
issue_context.analysis: The use cases and deficiencies are concrete enough to justify engineering design rather than another information request. The related #41879 is partial conceptual overlap, not a safe basis to close this more detailed proposal as a duplicate.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue, automated triage, labels, timeline, and all digest references; no owner or implementation PR exists.
Inspected src/modules/MouseUtils/MousePointerCrosshairs/dllmain.cpp: gliding is a 0–4 state machine with a single activation shortcut and fixed travel/delay settings.
Compared #41879, which asks for directional commands and multi-screen use but lacks the relative-origin and complete runtime-control scope here.
